h1: AI agents and automations for HR teams
answer: HR teams hand off the copying first: approved leave onto the team calendar, new hires announced, a daily applicant summary.
Captain builds these on Keka, Personio, Greenhouse and more; decisions about people stay with people.

jobs.title: A daily applicant summary
jobs.body: Each morning, an AI agent reads yesterday’s new applications in Greenhouse or Recruitee and sends you a short list by role, with what stands out in each.
jobs.ask: Set up an AI agent that every weekday at 9:00 reads yesterday’s new applications in Greenhouse and sends me a short summary by job

jobs.title: Brief interviewers
jobs.body: When an interview is scheduled in Greenhouse, send the interviewer the candidate’s name, role and time. Each email waits for your yes today.
jobs.ask: Set up an automation: when a new interview is scheduled in Greenhouse, email the interviewer the candidate, the job and the time

jobs.title: Answer staff policy questions
jobs.body: An AI agent reads questions sent to hr@ and drafts answers from your handbook in its memory; it leaves anything personal or sensitive for you.
jobs.ask: Set up an AI agent that reads new emails to hr@, drafts answers to policy questions from our handbook, and leaves anything personal for me

faqs.q: Which HR apps does it work with?
faqs.a: Those in viaSocket’s catalog, including Keka, Personio, Greenhouse, Recruitee, Breezy HR, Teamtailor, Calamari and RotaCloud. What you can build depends on each app’s triggers and actions.
Connect only the apps a job needs and keep personal details out of shared channels. Say in the job what may be shared; the AI agents ask before sending anything to people.
It can summarise applications for you. Decisions about people should stay with people, and in many places the law says so.

faqs.q: What does it not do yet?
faqs.a: BambooHR is not in viaSocket’s catalog today, so it cannot be connected. It does not run payroll, and it never decides on hiring, pay or leave; those stay with people. Some HR apps have few triggers (Keka has one), so jobs on them run on a schedule rather than the moment something changes. Posting to a team Slack channel waits for your approval today.
